text.p: Shareholders of Commercial International Bank (CIB) on Thursday gave the board clearance to raise up to 900 million pounds ($265 million) by issuing Egyptian pound or foreign currency bonds or floating rate notes, General Manager Adel El-Labban told Reuters.
The approval was not linked to any specific bond issue proposal but the bank does intend to make use of the option some time before the end of 1998, he said.
"There was unanimous approval of our funding proposals but this is not for a specific subvention," he said.
"We do anticipate using it, in one or more transactions. To expand, we have to diversify our sources of funding," he added. "Obviously we will try to get the most advantageous terms."

The 900 million pounds is slightly short of the amount the bank could raise through bonds under the rules set up the state's Capital Market Authority (CMA), based on 950 million pounds as the bank's net worth at the end of 1995, he said.
The proposal put to shareholders was for Egyptian pound instruments up to a value of 500 million pounds and foreign currency instruments up to the equivalent of 400 million pounds.
